Radiology departments and imaging centers operate in the same way airlines did in 1981, when airline companies had no access to operational data such as jet engine performance, wind statistics, etc.  Similarly, imaging facilities today critically lack access to operational data to manage their multi-million-dollar MRI scanners, leading to a true operational black hole and decisions based on gut feeling instead of data.

AI promised to revolutionize diagnosis in Radiology, but adoption has been slow with minimal impact on patient care in many clinical scenarios.  Quantivly instead focuses on an urgent problem of discovering operational patterns and help optimize operations, increase patient access, and improve patient satisfaction.
